question: What distinguishes the body from other objects established by consciousness?
premises: The body has a special status among things established by consciousness.
It is prior to all other objects that can be established.
Other things may also be identified with, but that identity is not known in the same way.
inference: The body is distinct because it serves as the primary basis for all further acts of establishment by consciousness.
uncertainties: The final clause is compressed and could also be read as emphasizing non-recognition of identity in other cases.
plain_english: The body is distinct because it comes first among all things that consciousness establishes. Other things may also be identified with, but that is not known in the same foundational way.
